clue.text: Go right out of fashion

indicators.note: 'right out of fashion' says the letter for right is removed from the word for fashion

parts.note: a fashion is a trend

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave a style that has fallen out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' tells you to take R away from TREND. 'Go' is the definition, in the sense of prices going, or tending, upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to incline or move in a direction, as in things going a certain way.

clue.text: Idle person who's objectionable throughout

parts.note: a tick is a contemptible person in British slang
over can mean throughout, as in all over the world

explanation.surface: A lazy person who is unpleasant all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' is a verb here: an engine that ticks over runs slowly without doing work.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine running slowly while disengaged is said to idle.

clue.text: Barrier about to be lifted for traveller

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means turned upwards, so both words are read backwards

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
on means about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A barrier is about to be raised for someone passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be lifted' turns DAM + ON upwards, reading NO MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer with no fixed home is a traveller.

clue.text: Middle English tirade about church? There's one in The Canterbury Tales

definitions.text: There's one in The Canterbury Tales

indicators.note: 'tirade about church' puts the tirade round the church word, cut open to hold it

parts.note: a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A medieval-English rant against the church, as found among Chaucer's pilgrims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CH inside RANT, giving RCHANT, after ME. The Merchant is one of Chaucer's storytelling pilgrims in The Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's pilgrims include a trader who tells his own tale, so this is an example of one of the pilgrims.

clue.text: Rabbit outside hole caught by competent one, entirely on the quiet

indicators.note: 'Rabbit outside' means the rabbit's letters surround all that follows

parts.note: cony is an old word for a rabbit

indicators.note: 'hole caught by competent' means the hole sits inside the word for competent

parts.note: fit means capable, competent
a den is an animal's hole or lair
I is the Roman numeral for one
all means wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: A rabbit burrow is quietly guarded by a capable creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' puts DEN inside FIT for FIDENT; add I and ALL, and 'outside' wraps CONY round the lot. 'Rabbit' also tempts as CON or chatter, but only CONY fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something privately, in secret, is saying it on the quiet.

clue.text: Detest mania to be given a makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hates the idea of a craze being restyled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a makeover' rearranges MANIA TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe, so it means detest.

clue.text: Ferry to catch

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferry someone is to transport them, and to catch a fish or a ball is to seize it; both are senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Paper containing list with much info excited spy

indicators.note: 'Paper containing' means the paper's letters go round the rearranged material

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newspaper's long list of revelations stirs up a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges LIST and MUCH INFO into IFTHCOLUMNIS, and 'containing' puts it inside FT; 'with' only joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor working secretly within a country for its enemy is a kind of spy.

clue.text: Crew and passengers, far off, coming to great river

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers

indicators.note: 'far off' says those three letters come off the word for passengers

parts.note: fares are paying passengers
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Travellers on a distant voyage reach a great river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far off' looks like distance but removes FAR from FARES, leaving ES. The Ganges is India's great sacred river.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian waterway is one of the world's mighty rivers.

clue.text: A key element in one's performance in the opening number

definitions.text: A key element in one's performance in the opening number

parts.words: A key element in one's performance in the opening number
parts.note: the clue reads like a theatre review of a show's first song, but describes a device that opens when the right sequence of numbers is dialled, with no key

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises a crucial part of a performer's work in the show's first song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening number' sounds like the first song in a show, but here it is a number that opens something; 'key element' hints that it replaces a key.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of fastening opens to a remembered sequence of digits, which plays the part a key would otherwise play.

clue.text: Veteran recalled for example being in at Lord's in fantastic form

indicators.note: 'for example being in' puts the reversed abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
the words 'at Lord's' are put into a fantastic new form, that is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder, S included

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: An old cricketer is remembered playing brilliantly at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fantastic form' rearranges AT LORDS into OLDSTAR; 'recalled' turns EG into GE, and 'being in' puts it inside before the final R. Lord's is a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand, someone long experienced in a field, is a veteran.

clue.text: With some visibility returning a bird can be seen

indicators.note: returning tells you the letters taken are read backwards
'some visibility' means only part of that word's letters are taken

explanation.surface: In clearer weather, a bird can be spotted coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run of letters inside visibility, SIBI, and 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-billed wading bird is a type of bird, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Accomplish opening of stately property

parts.note: to effect something is to accomplish it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone gains the entrance to a grand stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' takes the first letter, S, of stately. 'property' means personal belongings here, not real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal possessions are called one's belongings or chattels, as in the deceased's goods.

clue.text: Fine trick involves cutting up foil

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: 'trick involves' means the trick's letters wrap round what follows

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a cutting remark is a tart, sharp one

explanation.surface: A clever trick slices up some wrapping foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TART into TRAT, and 'involves' puts it inside RUSE, after F. 'foil' is a verb: to thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart it, to stop it succeeding.

clue.text: King surrounded by gazing people, like fairytale emperor?

indicators.note: 'King surrounded by' means the king's letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: starers are people who gaze
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch amid a staring crowd, as in the story of the emperor's new clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Andersen's tale the emperor parades in invisible clothes, naked before his gawping subjects; 'starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor wore nothing at all, so he was completely bare, in British slang.

clue.text: Sea creature of note in gripping record

indicators.note: 'gripping record' says the note and 'in' hold the record word between them

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale
an LP is a long-playing record
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notable sea creature holds a vinyl record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts LP inside DOH + IN, giving DO-LP-HIN; 'of' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This intelligent marine mammal is a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Understanding touch by one connected with medical department

parts.note: a pat is a light touch
I is the Roman numeral for one
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A caring touch from someone working in a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'connected with' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient and understanding are both synonyms for tolerant, as in a forbearing teacher.

clue.text: Around beginning of action criticise mother country

indicators.note: 'Around beginning of action' says the following words go round the first letter of action

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone criticises their mother just as the action starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts A, from 'beginning of action', between PAN and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American state crossed by a famous canal is a country.

clue.text: Cash dispenser with nothing in, or tiny quantity

indicators.note: 'with nothing in' puts the zero letter inside the cash machine
'with nothing in' puts the zero letter inside the cash machine

parts.note: ATM is an automated teller machine, a cash dispenser
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An empty cash machine leaves you with barely anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element is used figuratively for a very small amount.

clue.text: House wine endlessly regiment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'House wine endlessly regiment (9)': LANCASTER is ASTI less its end inside LANCERS less its end, but the held clue has no container indicator and only one 'endlessly', so a word seems lost in the OCR and no scan or reprint gives it

clue.text: Call, making claim

explanation.walkthrough: 'making' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to name or style them, and a legal right to property is a claim or entitlement.

clue.text: Exercises requiring energy aboard American ship

indicators.note: 'energy aboard American ship' puts the energy letter on board, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes American naval vessels
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Workouts need stamina on a US naval vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' only links; 'Exercises' is a verb, as in exercises a right.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a power or right is to employ it.

clue.text: Dish is attached to residence, disrupting period character to a large extent

indicators.note: 'disrupting' means the joined words break into the following pair, splitting them apart

parts.note: a span is a period of time

indicators.note: only a large part of the word is kept, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a letter is a written character
taken as written
a home is a residence

explanation.surface: A homeowner's addition breaks up a period piece considerably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is attached to residence' gives IS + HOME; 'disrupting' puts it between SPAN and LETTE, which is LETTER with its last letter dropped by 'to a large extent'.
explanation.definitionFit: This potato and egg tortilla from Spain is a dish.

clue.text: Apple of small size pinched by cheat

indicators.note: something pinched by another is held tightly inside it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a cheat
wee means small, from Scots

explanation.surface: A little apple is stolen by a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched by' looks like theft but means held inside: WEE goes into STING.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeting is an old variety of sweet-tasting apple.

clue.text: Imbroglio Holmes soon comprehends

indicators.note: comprehends means takes in or includes, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes will soon understand a tangled situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehends' looks like understanding but means contains: the letters run across 'HolMES Soon'.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused, embarrassing muddle.
